concept.name: Test Doubles & Mocks

relationships.description: Connects Test Doubles & Mocks to contract testing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Test doubles replace real collaborators with controlled stand-ins (dummies, stubs, spies, mocks, and fakes) so unit and integration suites run in milliseconds without live networks, payment gateways, or flaky third-party sandboxes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Prefer stateful in-memory fakes and HTTP contract stubs (like WireMock) over over-specified mocks; mocking internal collaborators couples tests to implementation details and breaks refactoring.

concept.whyItMatters: Production services depend on PostgreSQL, Kafka, Stripe, and internal gRPC APIs that are slow, rate-limited, or non-deterministic under test. Without disciplined test doubles, a 2,000-test CI suite either takes 45 minutes against shared staging environments or fails randomly on network blips. Conversely, undisciplined mocking creates brittle tests that pass 100% while production crashes on serialization mismatches or SQL dialect bugs.
whenToUse: Isolating domain logic from non-deterministic boundaries like system clocks (`Clock.fixed()`), UUID generators, or external payment/SMS webhooks (Stripe `/v1/payment_intents`, Twilio).
Simulating rare infrastructure fault conditions—HTTP 429 rate limits, TLS handshake timeouts, or Kafka broker `NotLeaderOrFollower` errors—that cannot be reliably triggered against live sandboxes.
Replacing slow I/O repositories in fast unit suites (<10 ms per test) using an in-memory Fake that enforces the same uniqueness and state-transition invariants as production.
whenNotToUse: Testing SQL queries, ORM mappings, or database migrations—mocking `EntityManager` or `JdbcTemplate` hides real PostgreSQL `JSONB`, index, and constraint bugs that Testcontainers catches.
Mocking pure value objects, DTOs, or internal helper classes within the same module, which turns refactoring into a rewrite of `verify()` assertions.
Validating wire-format compatibility with an external API unless the stub's responses are backed by recorded contract tests (e.g., Pact or OpenAPI schema validation).
keyPoints: Gerard Meszaros's 5-type taxonomy separates state verification (Dummy, Stub, Fake) from behavior verification (Spy, Mock), each carrying different coupling costs.
Fakes implement working, lightweight logic (e.g., an in-memory `ConcurrentHashMap` repository enforcing unique email constraints), whereas Stubs return canned answers without logic.
Mocks pre-program expectations and fail the test if exact method calls, arguments, or invocation counts are not met—making them the highest-coupling double.
Classicist (Detroit-school) testing mocks only across architectural boundaries (network, disk, time), while Mockist (London-school) testing mocks every collaborator.
Boundary stubs like WireMock or `responses` must be paired with contract assertions or periodic replay against staging so schema drift does not silently invalidate the suite.

examples.title: Stripe Payment Gateway Fault Injection with WireMock
examples.scenario: An order checkout service calls `POST https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents` with an `Idempotency-Key` header and must retry twice on HTTP 503 with exponential backoff, then fail fast on HTTP 402 Card Declined.
examples.outcome: Using WireMock's stateful scenario API, the test returns two 503 responses followed by a 200 JSON payload and asserts `WireMock.verify(3, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/v1/payment_intents")).withHeader("Idempotency-Key", matching(".+")))` in 35 ms—verifying real HTTP client serialization, headers, and retry math without hitting Stripe.

examples.title: Replacing Brittle Mockito Chains with an In-Memory Fake Repository
examples.scenario: A team had 140 JUnit tests stubbing `userRepo.findByEmail()`, `userRepo.save()`, and `Mockito.verify(userRepo, times(1)).save(argThat(...))` for an onboarding workflow.
examples.outcome: Switching to an `InMemoryUserRepository` fake backed by a `HashMap` with a unique-email check cut test setup code by 60%, caught a duplicate-email race bug that Mockito stubs had masked, and survived a repository API refactor with zero test rewrites.

tradeOffs.pro: In-memory fakes and Mockito mocks execute in 1–5 ms per test with zero Docker or network startup overhead.
tradeOffs.con: Fakes can drift from production behavior (e.g., missing PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT` semantics or isolation anomalies) unless verified by a thinner Testcontainers suite.

tradeOffs.pro: Mocks verify exact side effects on fire-and-forget boundaries like audit loggers or metrics emitters (`meterRegistry.counter(...).increment()`).
tradeOffs.con: Asserting internal call sequences (`InOrder`) breaks tests whenever implementation internals are optimized or reordered without changing observable outputs.

tradeOffs.pro: Hand-rolled fakes require zero reflection/bytecode proxies, run cleanly under GraalVM native tests, and are reused across dozens of test files.
tradeOffs.con: Maintaining fakes for complex interfaces with 20+ methods adds boilerplate unless interfaces are kept narrow (Interface Segregation Principle).

failureModes.name: Mock-Induced False Confidence (Tautological Tests)
failureModes.description: Tests mock both the input repository and the downstream publisher, asserting only that the mock returned what it was told to return while production fails on a `NullPointerException` in real deserialization.
failureModes.mitigation: Restrict mocks to true external I/O boundaries and run at least one vertical slice integration test per endpoint using real serialization and Testcontainers.

failureModes.name: Schema & Contract Drift
failureModes.description: An upstream microservice renames `customer_id` to `account_id` in its JSON response, but local WireMock stubs still return `customer_id`, keeping CI green until production throws 500s.
failureModes.mitigation: Validate stub payloads against shared OpenAPI/Protobuf schemas or Pact contracts in CI so breaking provider changes fail the build immediately.

failureModes.name: Over-Specified Interaction Coupling
failureModes.description: Refactoring a batch lookup from N calls to `getUser(id)` into 1 call to `getUsers(ids)` breaks 80 unit tests that used `verify(client, times(N)).getUser(...)`.
failureModes.mitigation: Assert observable state outcomes and final domain events rather than internal collaborator call counts; reserve `verify()` for strict side-effect boundaries.

failureModes.name: Leaky Shared Fake State
failureModes.description: A singleton `InMemoryOrderRepository` shared across parallel JUnit 5 or pytest workers retains records from previous tests, causing order-dependent flakiness.
failureModes.mitigation: Instantiate fresh fake instances per test case (`@BeforeEach` / pytest function fixture) and forbid mutable static state in test doubles.

commonMistakes: Mocking types you do not own (like `HttpClient` or `JdbcTemplate` directly) instead of wrapping them in a thin domain adapter interface.
Using `any()` matchers everywhere in `verify()`, which allows silently passing `null` or malformed arguments without failing the test.
Writing 30 lines of `when(...).thenReturn(...)` setup per test—a clear signal that the class under test has too many responsibilities or needs a Fake.
Leaving `verifyNoMoreInteractions()` on mocks, which breaks unrelated tests whenever a new logging or metrics call is added.
Replacing SQL/NoSQL integration tests entirely with in-memory fakes, missing query syntax errors, transaction rollbacks, and constraint violations.

sections.content:
## The idea

Every automated test sits on a spectrum between **isolation** (fast, deterministic, pinpoint failure localization) and **fidelity** (exercising real SQL engines, TCP sockets, and serialization). **Test doubles**—coined by Gerard Meszaros as the umbrella term for *Dummy, Stub, Spy, Mock, and Fake*—let you control where a test sits on that spectrum.

Instead of letting a unit test open a TLS socket to Stripe or spin up a 30-second database container, you substitute a collaborator that implements the same port/interface. The critical architectural skill is choosing *which* kind of double to use and *where* to draw the boundary: mock or fake only at architectural seams (network, disk, clock, randomness), never between cohesive domain objects.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider a Java `RefundService.issueRefund(orderId, amount)` method that collaborates with three dependencies: `OrderRepository` (PostgreSQL), `PaymentGateway` (Stripe HTTP API), and `AuditLogger` (Kafka event emitter).

1. **Dummy (`CorrelationId` or unused `Tracer`)**: Passed to satisfy a constructor signature when the test path does not inspect tracing metadata.
2. **Fake (`InMemoryOrderRepository`)**: Stores `Order` records in a `HashMap<OrderId, Order>`, validates that `refundedAmount <= totalAmount`, and throws `DuplicateRefundException` on double-refunds—giving realistic state transitions in <1 ms.
3. **Stub (`StubPaymentGateway` or WireMock)**: Configured to return `GatewayResult.declined("insufficient_funds")` or HTTP `503` so the test deterministically exercises the compensation branch without calling Stripe.
4. **Spy / Mock (`AuditLogger`)**: Records emitted `AuditEvent` objects (Spy) or asserts `verify(auditLogger).logRefundAttempt(orderId, DECLINED)` (Mock) because the audit log is a fire-and-forget side effect with no return value.

sections.content:
## Detroit vs. London School & Coupling

Two major philosophies govern how aggressively teams use test doubles:

- **Detroit (Classicist) School**: Treat a "unit" as a cohesive behavior, not a single class. Use real domain objects together and introduce doubles *only* at shared mutable boundaries (databases, HTTP clients, system clocks). Tests remain resilient when you extract or inline helper classes.
- **London (Mockist) School**: Isolate every class from all collaborators using mocks (`@Mock` in Mockito, `unittest.mock.MagicMock` in Python). While this pinpoints which class broke, it creates tight coupling to method signatures and encourages anemic tests that mirror the implementation line-for-line.

In modern microservice architectures, a **hybrid boundary-first** approach wins: Classicist inside the domain core, WireMock/Testcontainers at network and persistence edges, and strict Mocks/Spies only for fire-and-forget side effects.

## Test Double Taxonomy & Selection Matrix

| Double Type | Has Working Logic? | Verification Style | Typical Tooling | Best Use Case | Primary Risk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dummy** | No (empty/no-op) | None | `null`, `NoOpTracer` | Satisfying unused constructor/method parameters | NullPointerException if code path unexpectedly touches it |
| **Stub** | No (canned returns) | State (indirect) | Mockito `when()`, WireMock | Returning fixed HTTP 200/429 payloads or `Clock.fixed()` | Canned data drifts from real API schema |
| **Spy** | Optional (wraps real) | Behavior (post-hoc) | `Mockito.spy()`, `sinon.spy()` | Asserting audit log or metric calls after execution | Partial mocking of SUT hides design coupling |
| **Mock** | No (pre-programmed) | Behavior (expectations) | Mockito `verify()`, `unittest.mock` | Verifying exact side effects on external ports | Brittle tests coupled to internal call order |
| **Fake** | Yes (simplified) | State | `InMemoryRepo`, H2/SQLite | Fast CRUD, uniqueness, and state-machine tests | Semantic divergence from production DB (e.g., locks, JSONB) |

## Failure modes

1. **Partial Mock Trap (`@Spy` on SUT)**: Spying on the class under test to stub one private-adjacent method often bypasses initialization or causes infinite recursion in proxies. Extract the collaborator into its own class instead.
2. **Async & Concurrency Blindness**: In-memory fakes rarely reproduce PostgreSQL `SERIALIZABLE` conflicts, row-level locks, or Kafka consumer rebalancing. Always back critical concurrency paths with a dedicated Testcontainers test.
3. **Unverified Mock Return Defaults**: Python's `MagicMock` silently returns truthy child `MagicMock` objects for misspelled attributes (e.g., `client.asert_called()` or `resp.status_code`), causing tests to pass vacuously. Always pass `spec=RealClass` or `autospec=True`.
4. **Over-Mocked Serialization**: Mocking the `ObjectMapper` or HTTP client skips testing Jackson `@JsonProperty` annotations, date formats, and enum unknown-value handling.

## Contract Testing & Anti-Drift Guardrails

To prevent stubs and fakes from lying about production dependencies:

- **Contract Tests for Fakes**: Write an abstract `OrderRepositoryContractTest` suite containing 10–15 behavioral assertions (save, duplicate key, optimistic lock conflict, pagination) and run it against *both* `InMemoryOrderRepository` and `PostgresOrderRepository` (via Testcontainers). Any semantic drift fails immediately.
- **Consumer-Driven Contracts (Pact / OpenAPI)**: Generate WireMock stubs directly from OpenAPI 3.1 specs or Pact files verified by the provider service in CI.
- **Strict Mock Modes**: Use `Mockito.strictness(Strictness.STRICT_STUBS)` (default in JUnit 5 `MockitoExtension`) to fail on unused stubs, and `create_autospec(Class, spec_set=True)` in Python to reject invalid attribute access.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Draw test double boundaries strictly at I/O seams (DB, HTTP, Queue, Clock, RNG)—keep domain objects real.
- [ ] Prefer a reusable **Fake** over repeating `when(...).thenReturn(...)` setups across 5+ tests.
- [ ] Run a shared **Contract Test** against both your in-memory Fake and the real Testcontainers adapter.
- [ ] Enable strict stubbing (`MockitoExtension` in Java, `autospec=True` in Python) to catch dead stubs and typos.
- [ ] Use **WireMock** (or `respx`/`responses`) for HTTP clients so serialization, headers, and timeouts are actually exercised.
- [ ] Verify HTTP stubs against OpenAPI/Pact schemas in CI to prevent silent contract drift.

interviewProblems.title: Test Doubles & Mocks
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Test Doubles & Mocks. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Test doubles replace real collaborators with controlled stand-ins (dummies, stubs, spies, mocks, and fakes) so unit and integration suites run in milliseconds without live networks, payment gateways, or flaky third-party sandboxes.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: InMemoryOrderRepo applies the primary invariant and coordinates with WireMock / Spy.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, WireMock / Spy experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Restrict mocks to true external I/O boundaries and run at least one vertical slice integration test per endpoint using real serialization and Testcontainers.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Prefer stateful in-memory fakes and HTTP contract stubs (like WireMock) over over-specified mocks; mocking internal collaborators couples tests to implementation details and breaks refactoring.
Avoid trap: Mocking types you do not own (like `HttpClient` or `JdbcTemplate` directly) instead of wrapping them in a thin domain adapter interface.
Avoid trap: Using `any()` matchers everywhere in `verify()`, which allows silently passing `null` or malformed arguments without failing the test.

When to reach for it: Isolating domain logic from non-deterministic boundaries like system clocks (`Clock.fixed()`), UUID generators, or external payment/SMS webhooks (Stripe `/v1/payment_intents`, Twilio).

When to reach for it: Simulating rare infrastructure fault conditions—HTTP 429 rate limits, TLS handshake timeouts, or Kafka broker `NotLeaderOrFollower` errors—that cannot be reliably triggered against live sandboxes.

putItTogether.title: Putting Test Doubles Mocks Together
putItTogether.summary: Prefer stateful in-memory fakes and HTTP contract stubs (like WireMock) over over-specified mocks; mocking internal collaborators couples tests to implementation details and breaks refactoring.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Test Doubles Mocks before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Using WireMock's stateful scenario API, the test returns two 503 responses followed by a 200 JSON payload and asserts `WireMock.verify(3, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/v1/payment_intents")).withHeader("Idempotency-Key", matching(".+")))` in 35 ms—verifying real HTTP client serialization, headers, and retry math without hitting Stripe.
